errors.description: The single topstitch line is on the WRONG SIDE of the buttons - mirrored relative to the drawing. Measured on the gridded 5x magnification of the placket (crop x=330-530): soft inner crease at x=362, button centre x=408 with a 40 px diameter, single dashed stitch line at x=442-444, and a hard shadowed centre-front fold at x=450-455. Scaling by the 1.1 cm button (40 px = 1.1 cm, 1 cm = 36.4 px), the stitch sits only 0.25 cm inside the centre-front edge while the inboard 2.2 cm of the placket carries no stitching at all. The bottom crop confirms the hard line at x=452 is the centre-front edge: the hem topstitch runs continuously across it at the same height on both sides, and the placket band 362-452 drops below that hem line as a separate applied band.
errors.expected: Order across the placket from the centre front inward must be: clean unstitched front fold, then the buttons, then the single topstitch line well inboard. In the drawing (589 px wide) the solid red front edge is at x=217, button centres at x=233, and the single dashed red stitch line at x=255 - edge-to-button 0.88 cm, edge-to-stitch 2.09 cm against an 1.1 cm button.
errors.actual: Order is: centre-front fold at 452, stitch at 443 (0.25 cm inside it), then buttons at 408, then an unstitched 2.2 cm of placket running inboard to a bare crease at 362. The stitch and the buttons have swapped sides.
errors.correction: Move the single stitch line to the inboard side of the buttons, about 2.1 cm from the clean centre-front fold, and leave the front fold itself unstitched.

errors.description: Button offset from the centre-front edge is oversize. Measured against the 1.1 cm button as scale, the button centre sits 1.2 cm from the front fold; the drawing places it 0.88 cm from the front edge.

errors.correction: Set the button line closer to the front fold, reproducing the drawn offset.

The drawing is genuine and does depict placket topstitching, so it is usable, but a human should confirm the two options are meant to share it - if they are actually different constructions, one of them has the wrong illustration and no amount of photography will fix that.

TRAJECTORY. Attempt 1: collar-and-chest framing, and the placket double-topstitched with the button centred between two parallel stitch lines at x=390 and x=464 - the generic double-topstitched placket, a sibling option on the same field. Attempt 2: the correction fixed both - framing moved to the lower front with the collar excluded, and exactly ONE stitch line appeared, in the CORRECT order (front fold 240, buttons 294, stitch 338). Its remaining faults were a placket 3.0 cm wide against the drawn 2.1 cm, buttons 1.65 cm from the fold against the drawn 0.88 cm, a peeled-back triangular flap at the placket bottom, and trousers in the lower frame. Attempt 3: the flap is gone, the hem is one clean continuous curve, the trousers are down to a sliver, and edge-to-stitch is now 2.22 cm against the drawn 2.09 cm - but the stitch line moved to the wrong side of the buttons, which is a worse error than any it fixed.

FOR A HUMAN PICKER: attempt 2 is better than attempt 3 on the single most important axis. Attempt 2 has the stitch on the correct side of the buttons and only proportion errors plus a bottom-corner defect; attempt 3 has clean construction and near-perfect edge-to-stitch distance but mirrors the defining relationship. This is the oscillation pattern - the correction fixed what it named and broke what it did not. Neither is shippable; if one must be chosen as a base for a future pass, choose attempt 2.

What I did NOT verify: the literal 0.1 cm stitch-to-edge offset. In every attempt the stitch runs on flat cloth with no folded edge adjacent to it at readable scale, so the 0.1 cm dimension is not measurable from these renders and I am not asserting it.
